description: A dual CV sequencer whose fifteen step knobs form two eight-step rings sharing one knob, with either voice able to jump from one ring to the other

params.text: Returns both voices to the shared first step
Sets the voltage of the first step of both rings, read by whichever voice has reached that step
Sets the voltage of that step of the blue ring, spread over the blue range and quantized while the blue Planck constant is on
Sets the voltage of that step of the yellow ring, spread over the yellow range and quantized while the yellow Planck constant is on
Sets the chance of a voice jumping to the other ring when a jump is offered, none fully anticlockwise and certain fully clockwise
Steps the voltage that voice's step knobs cover: 0-1V, minus 1V to 2V or minus 2V to 3V while its Planck constant is on, and plus or minus 1V, 5V or 10V while it is off
Offers a jump to the other ring at every step instead of only at the last step of a ring
Steps which clock advances that voice: the global clock, that voice's own local clock, or both of them
Quantizes that voice's output to semitones, and narrows the voltage its range covers
Makes a pulse at a local clock input advance its voice by a weighted random 1 to 8 steps instead of one
Returns both voices to the shared first step whenever run is switched on
Advances both voices by one step for each press

inputs.text: A rising edge here advances every voice set to take the global clock, unless that voice's local clock fired on the same sample
A rising edge here advances that voice while it is set to take its local clock, by one step, or by a weighted random 1 to 8 steps while uncertainty is on
A trigger here starts and stops both voices
A rising edge here returns both voices to the shared first step
Every volt here adds a tenth to the chance of a jump, on top of the probability knob
Sets the range of that voice and overrides its button: 1V and above the widest, minus 1V and below the narrowest, and between them the middle one
Sets which clock advances that voice and overrides its button: 1V and above the global clock, minus 1V and below the local one, and between them both
A trigger here turns the jump at every step on and off
A trigger here turns the random step count on and off

outputs.text: The voltage of the knob the blue voice has reached, in whichever ring it is travelling
The voltage of the knob the yellow voice has reached, in whichever ring it is travelling
A 1ms 10V pulse each time that voice jumps from one ring to the other

notes: the sequence does not advance until a clock arrives; the module comes up running, and the run button stops and starts it
with the jump probability at zero the module is two independent eight-step sequences, and with it fully clockwise the two voices share one sixteen-step sequence
the step button advances the sequence whether or not the module is running, which is how the step voltages are set and heard one at a time while it is stopped
